speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked﻿	the Minister for Health what is the Ministry doing to promote experimentation and innovation in the eldercare sector so as to encourage care models that provide greater privacy for dementia patients in a space-efficient way.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The Ministry of Health (MOH) has been making innovations in care for our elderly, including those with dementia, with our partners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The home is designed in the form of small "clusters".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Each cluster consists of bedrooms with a smaller number of beds compared to other nursing homes, sharing a common living space, including activity and dining area, as well as bathrooms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: This design allows for a smaller-scale and more familiar environment to support residents with dementia and yet promotes interaction among seniors and does not segregate or confine seniors in single rooms which may be more challenging in terms of monitoring and care.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: This design is the result of a brainstorming workshop with Ren Ci, facilitated by Dr Emi Kiyota, an environmental gerontologist based in the US, who is most noted for her work in championing Page: 15 the concept of the "Ibasho" or a place where seniors can live in safety, comfort and dignity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We have also implemented several dementia-friendly initiatives at our acute and community hospitals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The Institute of Mental Health (IMH) has renovated a dementia ward to create a more homely living environment which includes a garden designed to allow dementia patients to move around safely.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The ward includes a reminiscence room and a sensory room to provide dementia-specific therapy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Khoo Teck Puat Hospital (KTPH) is also operating a ward which is designed to have minimal distractions from the hospital environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: This is to provide better and more personalised care for dementia patients who may find the unfamiliar environment in a hospital disconcerting and stressful.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: St Luke's Hospital (SLH) and St Andrew's Community Hospital (SACH) have also introduced dementia-friendly wards which are designed to provide a more private and safer environment for dementia patients to move around, participate in group activities and interact with one another.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Staff in these wards received additional training in dementia care to provide care that is tailored to the unique needs and personality of each dementia patient.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Dementia care is evolving in Singapore and we are continually seeking to learn and experiment on better models.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Even in land-scarce Singapore, it is possible to design spaces that strike a balance between providing for the privacy and dignity of users and ensuring the cost-effectiveness and sustainability of the care model.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We will continue to learn and adopt new thinking into our local efforts in designing dementia care facilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: But good dementia care goes beyond the physical attributes of the care facility.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Good care has to come from quality hardware design, coupled with good care delivery.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: For example, Tsao Foundation offers a dementia home intervention service where they provide advice to caregivers on how to better care for their loved ones at home.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: NTUC Health and Thye Hua Kwan also provide elder-sitting services, where care staff accompany persons with dementia at their homes and engage them in activities according to their personal interests.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We have also worked with Tote Board to put in place a Community Healthcare Fund to support new pilots in the community, including in dementia care.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: These include Montfort Care's Happy Kopitiam programme which provides caregivers with education and support, while giving an avenue for caregivers and persons with dementia to participate in activities together and Alzheimer's Disease Association's Family of Wisdom programme where caregivers take part in the day care sessions with their loved ones with dementia and provide mutual support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The Government also provides funding support to further catalyse new models of care and ideas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The grant call attracted close to 40 proposals from multidisciplinary research teams that comprise clinicians, engineers, sociologists and care providers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We will continue to enhance the access, quality and affordability of care to seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We will partner our aged care providers to innovate and make eldercare better and more resource-effective.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I just have two supplementary questions, if I Page: 16 may.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: My second question is: would the Ministry consider initiating a process to develop an integrated national plan to cope with dementia, which will be an increasing problem in Singapore, along the lines of the Australian National Framework for Action on Dementia and the report of the Hong Kong Working Group on Dementia?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: First of all, let me say that MOH supports innovation on new models of care that will enhance care outcomes for the patients.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But we need to balance this against the need to ensure the long-term sustainability of the care models because our aged care needs will grow and, ultimately, subsidies come from taxes.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Due to the reduced ability of dementia patients to adapt to environmental stresses, smaller scale layouts which provide personal space and privacy would actually help the patients in terms of calming them and ensuring that they are not aggressive and there are no other negative social reactions.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But single beds, which is Jade Circle's proposal, do have their downsides.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For instance, there will be patients who would feel more isolated if they do not come out of their rooms.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And there are issues with safety, surveillance, monitoring because of line of sight by the care staff and, particularly so for patients with functional deficits, leading to limited independence or because of behavioural and psychological problems.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, there will be challenges not just with space constraints, but also manpower constraints.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Single rooms are not necessarily the magic pill to good quality dementia care.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have pointed out, good quality dementia care does not depend just on the physical attributes of the facility – of which layout of the bedroom is one aspect – but it also depends on the quality of the care delivery.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Having said that, we note that there will be instances where single rooms or twin-bedded rooms are needed for patients, say, with some behavioural issues.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: These are provided in our purpose-built nursing homes.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But having said that, as I have said, we do want to support innovative new models of care because we do want to experiment and learn and find better care models.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Then, we can learn lessons from this model and see if we can apply it to the rest of the sector.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: With regard to funding, as I have said, we need to ensure that the care models are sustainable because, at the end of the day, we know that ageing needs are going to grow and we do have limited resources, as well as manpower and space constraints, so we need to look at the different models of care and ensure that these are sustainable models and are cost-effective.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And there are actually subvention or subsidy to the individual patient, which is Page: 17 portable because it depends on which nursing home or which care they take up.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I also want to add that, at the end of the day, if you ask the elderly, their preferred option is to be cared for at home, not in an institution.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Nursing home should only be for those with higher care needs, as well as those with very low or no family and social support.
